title: Data on Employees who have been Supported by Jobs Support Scheme
what_it_is: Data on Employees who have been Supported by Jobs Support Scheme

sections.label: Jobs Support Scheme payouts
sections.summary: Over $16 billion of Jobs Support Scheme payouts went to more than 150,000 employers, supporting over two million local workers, with $15.5 billion to SMEs.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Since the introduction of the Jobs Support Scheme or JSS at the Unity Budget in February, over $16 billion of payouts have been disbursed to more than 150,000 employers.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This has helped to support the wages of over two million local workers. $15.5 billion of the JSS payouts went to SMEs.

sections.label: JSS revenue bands and review
sections.summary: JSS payouts and worker proportions are given by revenue band, and the Ministry says it lacks data on companies with no revenue drop but reviews its tiered approach.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: As for the breakdown by revenue bands – below $10 million, between $10 million and $100 million, between $100 million and $250 million, and above $250 million – the dollar payouts are: $5.8 billion, $4.0 billion, $1.6 billion, and $4.9 billion respectively.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The corresponding proportion of local workers supported by the JSS is: 46%, 24%, 9% and 21% respectively.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We do not have data on which companies had no drop in revenue in the first half of 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: As an alternative, we have made use of other sources of data, reports and industry feedback to provide different levels of JSS support to different sectors, based on the impact of COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In terms of the revenue requirement, may I ask if the Ministry would consider granting additional support to companies who may have suffered a sharper decline in revenues as opposed to some of the companies which is right now classified under Tier 3B, for example, which potentially may even have their revenues increased during this period, put more resources to companies which may have suffered a greater fall in revenues rather than from an overall sectoral approach.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: I think, as I mentioned in my reply, we do not collect the data in order to ease the administrative burden of firms in terms of the level of revenues to which they may have suffered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: But the tiered approach provides a fairly quick, fairly good approximation of the sectors and these measures are being reviewed, even as we speak.
